children.name: Crypturellus
children.description: The most diverse genus of tinamous, with many species found across Central and South America.

children.name: Crypturellus atrocapillus
children.description: The black-capped tinamou (Crypturellus atrocapillus) is a type of tinamou commonly found in the moist forest lowlands in subtropical and tropical regions.

children.name: Crypturellus bartletti
children.description: Bartlett's tinamou (Crypturellus bartletti) is a type of tinamou found in lowland forest in South America.

children.name: Crypturellus berlepschi
children.description: Berlepsch's tinamou (Crypturellus berlepschi) is a type of ground bird found in moist forest in northwestern Colombia and northwestern Ecuador.

children.name: Crypturellus boucardi
children.description: The slaty-breasted tinamou or Boucard's tinamou (Crypturellus boucardi) is a type of tinamou commonly found in lowland moist forests of Mexico and Central America.

children.name: Crypturellus brevirostris
children.description: The rusty tinamou or short-billed tinamou (Crypturellus brevirostris) is a type of tinamou commonly found in swamp forest in tropical regions of South America.

children.name: Crypturellus cinereus
children.description: The cinereous tinamou (Crypturellus cinereus), also known as brushland tinamou, is a type of ground bird found in swamp and lowland forests in northern South America. They have some localized names that have been used by the indigenous people such as in Amazonas where they are called inambu-pixuna, and in Pará, Brazil where they are called nambu-sujo. Also, throughout their range they are called inhambu-preto. Cinereous tinamous have been around for many centuries. They are part of the oldest families of the world today and have fossils discovered dating back tens of millions of years. Their quick reflexes play a role in their ability to survive.

children.name: Crypturellus cinnamomeus
children.description: The thicket tinamou or rufescent tinamou (Crypturellus cinnamomeus) is a type of tinamou commonly found in moist forests in subtropical and tropical central Mexico.

children.name: Crypturellus duidae
children.description: The grey-legged tinamou (Crypturellus duidae), alternatively, the gray-legged tinamou, is a small ground-dwelling bird endemic to the neotropics. It is a rarely seen bird due to its small size and discreet appearance.

children.name: Crypturellus erythropus
children.description: The red-legged tinamou or red-footed tinamou, (Crypturellus erythropus) is a ground-dwelling bird found in the tropics and lower subtropics of northern South America.

children.name: Crypturellus kerriae
children.description: The Choco tinamou or Chocó tinamou (Crypturellus kerriae) is a type of tinamou found in lowland forest and montane forest in subtropical and tropical regions of Colombia and Panama.

children.name: Crypturellus noctivagus
children.description: The yellow-legged tinamou (Crypturellus noctivagus) is a species of tinamou found in wooded and shrubby habitats in tropical and subtropical eastern Brazil. This superficially quail-like bird has a grey-brown plumage and two easily separated subspecies. It has declined due to human activities, and is therefore listed as Near Threatened by the IUCN.

children.name: Crypturellus obsoletus
children.description: The brown tinamou (Crypturellus obsoletus) is a brownish ground bird found in humid lowland and montane forest in tropical and subtropical South America.

children.name: Crypturellus parvirostris
children.description: The small-billed tinamou (Crypturellus parvirostris) is a type of tinamou commonly found in dry savanna in Amazonian South America.

children.name: Crypturellus ptaritepui
children.description: The tepui tinamou (Crypturellus ptaritepui) is a type of ground bird found in montane moist forest on tepuis, in southeastern Venezuela.

children.name: Crypturellus soui
children.description: The little tinamou (Crypturellus soui) is a species of tinamou. It is found in Central and South America, as well as on the Caribbean island of Trinidad.

children.name: Crypturellus tataupa
children.description: The Tataupa tinamou (Crypturellus tataupa) is a type of tinamou commonly found in dry forest in subtropical and tropical regions in southeastern South America.

children.name: Crypturellus transfasciatus
children.description: The pale-browed tinamou (Crypturellus transfasciatus) is a type of tinamou found in tropical dry forests in Peru and Ecuador.

children.name: Crypturellus variegatus
children.description: The variegated tinamou (Crypturellus variegatus) is a type of tinamou commonly found in moist forest lowlands in subtropical and tropical regions of northern South America.

children.name: Eudromia
children.description: Distinguished by their elegant, forward-curving crests, these larger tinamous inhabit dry open country in southern South America. They are more social than other tinamous, often encountered in small coveys.

children.name: Eudromia elegans
children.description: The elegant crested tinamou or martineta tinamou (Eudromia elegans) is a medium-sized tinamou that can be found in southern Chile and Argentina in Shrubland. The bird has an omnivorous diet. This species is terrestrial due to their poor flying ability.

children.name: Eudromia formosa
children.description: The quebracho crested tinamou (Eudromia formosa) is a species of tinamou found in dry forest habitats in Paraguay and northern Argentina in South America.

children.name: Nothocercus

children.name: Nothocercus bonapartei
children.description: The highland tinamou or Bonaparte's tinamou (Nothocercus bonapartei) is a type of ground bird found in montane moist forest typically over altitude.

children.name: Nothocercus julius
children.description: The tawny-breasted tinamou (Nothocercus julius) is a type of ground bird found in montane moist forest. Their range is northwestern South America.

children.name: Nothocercus nigrocapillus
children.description: The hooded tinamou (Nothocercus nigrocapillus) is a type of ground bird found in forests of Bolivia and Peru.

children.name: Nothoprocta
children.description: A genus of medium-sized tinamous adapted to the open grasslands, scrublands and high-altitude puna of the Andes. Their mottled plumage offers superb camouflage against the rocky, arid landscapes they inhabit.

children.name: Nothoprocta perdicaria

children.name: Rhynchotus rufescens
children.description: The red-winged tinamou (Rhynchotus rufescens) is a medium-sized ground-living bird from central and eastern South America. Other common names for the species include perdiz grande, rufous tinamou, and ynambu.

children.name: Rhynchotus maculicollis
children.description: The huayco tinamou (Rhynchotus maculicollis), also known as waypu (Quechua) (also spelled guaipo, huaipo, guaypo, waypo, a name which is also applied for other Tinamidae species), is a species of bird found on grassy mountain ridges in the Andes of Bolivia and Argentina.

children.name: Taoniscus
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the smallest tinamou.

children.name: Taoniscus nanus
children.description: The dwarf tinamou (Taoniscus nanus), also known as the least tinamou, is a small, superficially partridge-like bird with short tail and wings, found only in Brazil.

children.name: Tinamotis
children.description: Tinamotis — a genus of tinamous in the family Tinamidae.

children.name: Tinamotis ingoufi
children.description: The Patagonian tinamou (Tinamotis ingoufi) also known as Ingouf's tinamou is a member of one of the most ancient groups of paleognath birds, the tinamous. This species is native to southern South America.

children.name: Tinamotis pentlandii
children.description: The puna tinamou, also known as Pentland's tinamou, is a member of the tinamou family. This species is native to the Andes Mountains in South America. The binomial name of the species commemorates the Irish natural scientist Joseph Barclay Pentland (1797–1873) by Nicholas Aylward Vigors in 1837.

children.name: Tinamus
children.description: The largest tinamou genus, comprising heavily-built, terrestrial forest birds with cryptic plumage and a distinctive curved bill. They are weak fliers but extremely difficult to spot on the forest floor.

children.name: Tinamus major
children.description: The great tinamou (Tinamus major) is a species of tinamou ground bird native to Central and South America.

children.name: Tinamus guttatus
